newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan refinery fire extinguished, one hurt.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan refinery fire extinguished, one hurt.

text.p: A fire and explosion hit the northern Taoyuan refinery of Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp on Thursday, officials said.
The blaze, which occurred in a hydro-desulfurisation unit that was closed for annual maintenance, was extinguished within an hour, refinery officials told Reuters by telephone.
One refinery worker suffered unspecified injuries that were not believed to be life-threatening, they said.
Executives said the fire affected a part of the refinery that processes residual oil.

State radio said some 200 firefighters and more than 30 pieces of firefighting equipment were mobilised to fight the fire. A headcount to ensure that all workers and firefighters were safe was still underway, it said.

The refinery, which mainly serves Taiwan's domestic market, is Chinese Petroleum's main production facility for jet fuel, turning out 60,000 tonnes of jet oil a month at peak capacity for the nearby Taipei international airport.
Investigators said they were trying to determine the cause of the initial fire, which triggered a series of hydrogen explosions in the hydro-desulfurisation unit, officials said.
The force of the blasts blew out windows in nearby residential areas, state radio said.

The accident at Taoyuan was the second to hit Taiwan's oil giant on Thursday, coming just hours after a two-minute power outage in southern Kaohsiung that forced a costly shutdown of its huge No.5 naphtha cracker and a score of affiliated plants.
The cracker and affected plants would be brought back to normal operation by Saturday, officials said.

The Taoyuan fire was the latest in a series of accidents at the refinery in the past year that have aroused public concern over the state firm's management -- and forced the sacking of its president and chairman in late 1996.
